items.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019
items.q: The interviewee discusses David Letterman's career moves, business ownership (World Wide Pants), and retirement actions, but does not describe a personal or professional relationship with him.

ctx.x: It was but no more unfortunately. When David Letterman — see Letterman was a unique animal that he was on NBC and then Jay Leno got the Tonight Show and Letterman got PO’d and he went to CBS and he started his own show. NBC wouldn’t let him take any of the rights or do anything. NBC owned Late Night. So when he moved to CBS David Letterman — did you ever see “World Wide Pants”? World Wide Pants was the corporation that Letterman owned. He owned the show instead of CBS owning it. When he retired he pulled every…
You should all just gather at his house someday, “David, we’ve got an idea for you.”

Yeah. He’s out in Montana, that’s where he is. Him and Tom Brokaw bought two farms in the middle of Montana back to back. So if you look at a map I think the whole middle of the state of Montana is owned by Letterman/Brokaw.
